name: What does a feasibility study cover before designing a custom home?

mainEntity.name: What should a home feasibility study include before I start designing a custom home in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should a home feasibility study include before I start designing a custom home in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A feasibility study is the early filter that tells you whether the project is practical before you spend heavily on full plans. It should review the site’s zoning, setbacks, buildable area, height restrictions, access, utility conditions, grading needs, drainage, and any neighborhood-specific constraints. For more complex sites, it may also flag the need for engineering, soils work, or additional approvals. The point is to identify the likely path, the probable budget range, and the biggest risks before the design becomes too advanced to change efficiently. Homeowners who skip this step often discover problems after they have already invested in drawings. A proper feasibility review can save time, money, and frustration by showing what is possible and what is not.
acceptedAnswer.description: A feasibility study should check zoning, setbacks, lot coverage, height limits, access, site constraints, utility conditions, and likely permit hurdles before full design begins. It helps determine whether the project is realistic and what the major risks will be.
